transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, they actually sent me here from occupational health at my job. They're saying my weight is dangerously low for someone running presses and doing fabrication all day. I didn't really see it that way, though. I honestly just thought I was getting leaner and more disciplined.
Have you lost weight recently without trying to, or has your weight loss been intentional through diet and exercise?

It was definitely intentional. I've been very careful about my diet. Most days, I just keep it to coffee before my early shift... then maybe half a protein bar on my lunch break. After work, I'll do yoga and just have a small bowl of vegetables. Honestly, if I eat more than that, it just makes the whole day feel completely out of control.
Can you tell me approximately how much you weigh now, and how tall you are?

I'm actually not entirely sure what my exact weight is right now. I don't keep a scale at the house—I mostly just go by how my work clothes fit, which is how I know I've leaned out. And for my height... I mean, I'm just average height. 

The occupational health nurse at work took all those measurements before they told me I had to come here, but I didn't really look at the numbers they wrote down.
Can you provide your current weight in pounds or kilograms and your height in feet/inches or meters?
Like I just said, I don't actually know my weight right now. I don't weigh myself. The nurse at work took it, but I didn't look at the scale or the paperwork. As for my height, I'm 5 foot 4.
Can you provide the weight measurement that the occupational health nurse recorded for you?

I really don't know what she wrote down. She didn't say it out loud, and... well, I just didn't look at the clipboard. They just told me I wasn't cleared for the floor and had to come see you. You might have it in whatever paperwork they sent over to your office, but I honestly couldn't tell you the number.
Can you tell me the exact weight in pounds or kilograms that the occupational health nurse recorded for you?
Look, I... I really don't know. Like I just said, she didn't tell me the number, and I didn't look at her paperwork. I just don't have that information to give you.
Can you give me the exact weight in pounds or kilograms that the occupational health nurse recorded for you?

I really don't know what to tell you. I've said it three times now—I don't know what weight she wrote down. I didn't see the number, she didn't say it, and I don't know what it is. I'm sorry, I just don't have that answer for you.
Can you tell me the exact weight in pounds or kilograms that the occupational health nurse recorded for you?

I'm really not sure why you keep asking me the exact same thing. Like I've been saying, I do not know the number. I didn't look at the scale, she didn't tell me what it was... so I just can't give you that information. You're going to have to look at whatever file she sent over to you, because I don't have the answer.
Can you tell me approximately what your body weight is in pounds or kilograms, even if it's just a rough estimate?

I honestly couldn't even give you a guess. I... I don't weigh myself at home, and like I said, I make it a point not to look at the numbers when I have to get checked for work. So I really just don't have any idea what it is right now, not even a rough estimate.
Can you tell me how you feel about the idea of gaining weight or becoming heavier?

The idea of it... honestly, it terrifies me. If I were to get on a scale and see the number go up even just a little bit, I think I would panic. It feels like if I gain weight, I'm going to lose all the control I've worked so hard for. I just... I can't end up heavy again. That's my biggest fear.
